mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.25% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a 5-day S&P 500 forward return of +1.5% due to expectations of accommodative policy sustaining equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative or less than +0.5% when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, labor market slack increases, reducing risk aversion and pushing the S&P 500 20-day forward return to -0.8% as investors anticipate weaker wage growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive or near zero when UNRATE declines by >0.2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% in the preceding quarter predict a +2% S&P 500 forward return over 60 trading days as demand growth supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST shows 3 consecutive monthly increases each ≥2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is ≤0% despite qualifying HOUST pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in INDPRO above 105 (index 2017=100) for two consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which is associated with a -1.2% S&P 500 20-day forward return as valuations adjust for tighter supply.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 2 consecutive months above 105
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive when INDPRO remains above 105 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by more than 0.5% in the same month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is +0.6%, reflecting dual signals of inflationary pressure and policy continuity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up >0.5% and CPIAUCSL up >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in the same direction by ≤0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment) of over 10,000 in a month coincides with a -1.3% S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates a weakening labor market and rising risk premia.
failure_condition: Forward return is positive or near zero when PAYEMS falls by ≤10,000.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at an annualized rate above 3% in the prior quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is +3.5%, reflecting optimism about robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is ≤0% despite quarterly GDPC1 growth >3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained RSAFS decline of 5% or more over three months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, resulting in a -2.1% S&P 500 20-day forward return as valuations correct.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive when RSAFS declines by <5% over 3 months.
